editorial:
Ever wonder how the world almost ran out of money in 2008? You get a front-row seat to the chaos in this movie, which follows the Treasury Secretary and other high-powered leaders as they scramble to stop a total economic collapse. It feels like a high-stakes race against time, with stressed-out people in suits arguing in boardrooms while the entire global market crashes around them. The vibe is tense and serious, making you feel the pressure these people were under when they had to make choices that affected millions of regular families.

What really works here is how it makes complicated banking stuff easy to understand. The acting is solid and keeps you locked in, though some parts might feel a bit slow if you aren't into finance. It is a great pick if you love true stories about power and panic.
endingExplained: The movie ends with the government stepping in to save the big banks with a massive bailout. You see that while the world economy was saved from a total crash, the people who caused the mess didn't really face any punishment. It wraps up by showing that the system stayed mostly the same. The final scenes leave you feeling a bit uneasy because the wealthy stayed wealthy while everyday people lost their homes.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about money and power
